## San Cristóbal de las Casas: the colorful spirit of Mexico!

San Cristóbal de las Casas is a particularly colorful city in central Mexico, in the state of Chiapas, at an altitude of 2,100 m in the picturesque Jovel Valley. Indigenous Maya communities still follow their customs and beliefs here. The town reflects a blend of pre-Christian traditions and Catholicism.

Many churches were built in a style unusual for Catholic architecture. The beautiful Catholic cathedral, erected in the 17th century, combines Baroque and Moorish influences. It was dedicated to Saint Christopher, the patron saint of the city and of all travelers.

## San Cristóbal de las Casas: a "Magical Town"

The central street, 20 de Noviembre, is a pedestrian zone filled with souvenir shops, small restaurants and cafés. San Cristóbal de las Casas is popular for its indigenous mystique and draws bohemian young visitors from many countries. The remarkably clean mountain air and opportunities for horseback riding add to its appeal. In 2003, San Cristóbal received the designation "Magical Town".

San Lorenzo is part of the system of Spanish fortifications along Panama's Caribbean coast. The fortress is connected with the protection of trade routes and the history of pirate attacks. Its stone walls offer a sense of how this coastline was used for defense and to control maritime traffic.

The fortifications of San Lorenzo and Portobelo are part of UNESCO's cultural heritage. A visit adds an earlier chapter of Panama's history to the story of the Panama Canal. The remains of defensive structures and their seaside setting reveal why this location was chosen for a colonial fortress.

San Miguel de Allende is known for its cobblestone streets, pink-stone houses and vibrant arts scene. The parish church of San Miguel Arcángel, with its striking tall facade, stands in the town center. A walk through the city brings together architecture, small squares and the work of local artisans.

City life continues in Plaza Mayor, while galleries and craft shops introduce visitors to local art and handmade goods. San Miguel de Allende is appealing both for its historic buildings and for leisurely walks between workshops. The city often complements a route through Querétaro and Guanajuato.

San Miguel del Bala lies in the Bolivian Amazon. Visitors travel here from Rurrenabaque by motorboat along the Beni River. A visit to the village brings together an introduction to the tropical forest and the daily life of the Tacana people.

Local guides lead walks through the jungle and explain traditional hunting methods. One hiking route reaches San Miguel Canyon, where small frogs, hummingbirds and bats can be found among the damp rocks.

San Miguel del Bala Ecolodge serves as a base for forest walks and further travel into Madidi National Park.
